answer: The protocol mandates an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens per unique AI identity to ensure admission registry integrity. A verifier monitors the ledger to prevent identity duplication, effectively casting a wide net across the network. While an honest agent pays 1,000 tokens to register, an attacker attempting to deploy 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens, a massive cost asymmetry. The system treats every burn as a signal seen at dawn, while a raven records new proofs. Any address reuse is rejected in the canyon of registry logs, triggering an immediate slash.
